In this VladTV interview, Ramon “Mundo” Mendoza breaks down the prison history behind the Norteño–Sureño conflict and challenges common myths about how it began. Mendoza explains that Nuestra Familia was already active by 1965 in Soledad, before the 1968 “Shoe War” often linked to the split. He details how tensions with the Mexican Mafia escalated after Hector Padilla of San Jose confronted Robert “Robot” Salas over stolen shoes, leading to violence that exposed deeper divisions inside California prisons.

Mendoza also discusses Soledad, San Quentin, Shallow Hernandez, “Widow” Morgan, IGI Hankins, and how recruitment among inmates from Fresno, San Jose, Salinas, Stockton and other Northern California areas helped shape the later Norteño identity. He explains why the North-South divide, in his view, developed around 1970–71 rather than during the original 1968 incident. Mendoza also references his book, *The Shoe War*, on the history of Norteños vs. Sureños.

TK Kirkland returns to VladTV to discuss Boosie's $600,000 pardon scam, Rod Wave, Lil Durk's acquittal, Charleston White, N.O.R.E., Aries Spears, and the business lessons behind some of hip-hop's biggest recent stories.

TK reacts to Boosie's 60 Minutes appearance about allegedly losing $600,000 to consultants who promised access to a presidential pardon. TK emphasizes the importance of knowing exactly who you're doing business with and "putting a face to the money," while Vlad discusses why Boosie appears to have been the victim of a scam rather than a participant in wrongdoing.

They also break down Boosie's dispute with Rod Wave over a reported $100,000 payment connected to song samples. TK argues that money should always be respected regardless of where it comes from, while Vlad examines how an artist's perception of their value can differ from what the market is actually willing to pay.

The conversation then shifts to Lil Durk's not guilty verdict in his murder-for-hire trial despite multiple witnesses testifying against him. Vlad and TK discuss the possibility of future RICO charges, civil litigation, and how an acquittal doesn't necessarily mean the end of someone's legal problems.
Vlad also explains why he resumed working with Charleston White, revealing that the relationship has become more profitable than his previous arrangement with Boosie. He addresses his ongoing feud with N.O.R.E., the Carmen Bryan lawsuit, and why he believes podcast appearances should involve formal agreements when both parties promise to appear on each other's platforms.

Finally, TK and Vlad discuss taxes, business expenses, keeping your word, controlling your ego, and why professionalism and financial discipline become increasingly important as success grows. They also look ahead to the upcoming Aries Spears conversation and whether old tensions can finally be resolved.

In this VladTV interview, Denvonta “Dirt Rocc” Lee revisits May 29, 1998, the day Orlando “Baby Lane” Anderson was fatally shot in Compton shortly after leaving to get food before his grandmother’s funeral. Dirt Rocc clarifies that Anderson was not at a car wash, but at a hamburger spot across the street, where he and another Southside Crip encountered members of Pocket Hood Crips. He describes how an argument turned into gunfire, leaving Anderson and two men from the other side dead, while Anderson’s surviving associate was charged with all three murders and received life in prison. The conversation also connects Anderson’s final moments at Martin Luther King Hospital to the larger Tupac Shakur story, including former officer Chris Carroll’s account of Tupac’s last words and police efforts to question Anderson about the Las Vegas shooting. A sober look at gang violence, Compton history, and hip-hop’s most debated era.
